name: CCBHC State Planning Grants (SM-26-016)
program: Cooperative agreements, Section 223 PAMA; ALN 93.829; Grants.gov opp 360982
heart: 12 states get $1M each to make clinics certification-ready, and the NOFO explicitly funds training/TA on implementing EBPs with fidelity — the 12 winners are the next CCBHC training market.
accounts_needed: None for More Therapy — contracted training/TA vendor inside a state's plan
scoring_map: A need 20; B implementation 35; C experience/staffing 30; D data 15
reason: not a fit — eligibility statutorily limited to state agencies (SMHA/SSA/SMA + DC); funds regulatory & reimbursement design, not clinical training, so no MORE budget line (team review 2026-08-06)

name: NIH HEAL — Translating Addiction Research into Practice (RFA-DA-27-016)
heart: NIH money a for-profit can hold directly, whose stated priority is exactly MORE's pitch: getting clinicians trained in and delivering evidence-based addiction treatment, with chronic-pain-comorbid SUD named as a priority. An R61 (train clinicians, pilot fidelity) into R33 (implementation trial) built around MORE dissemination.
accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + eRA Commons (SO + PI) + Grants.gov + ORCID — 6+ weeks
page_limit: Standard NIH page limits + 2-pp Timeline and Milestone Plan attachment
scoring_map: Standard NIH peer review; R33 transition is administrative against R61 milestones. NON-RESPONSIVE traps: solely testing new interventions, purely descriptive studies — frame as translation/implementation of the established MORE evidence base.

name: Maryland Opioid Restitution Fund 2027 (MOOR NOFA)
program: ORF Grant Program, CY2027-28 (settlement Exhibit E uses)
heart: Maryland settlement dollars, $1M ceiling per 2-year project, for evidence-based treatment and staff training — MORE rides as a named training/subcontract line in a nonprofit partner's application.
accounts_needed: Partner needs 501(c) letter, MD SDAT good standing, charity registration, 990, W-9; no SAM/Grants.gov
scoring_map: Staff eligibility screen → Evaluation Committee ranking (no published points). Must align with a settlement Exhibit E provision + a Project Focus Area; 'evidence-based substance use treatment is allowable' incl. co-occurring.

name: Alabama ADMH Opioid Settlement Round 4 (RFP 2027-04)
heart: Alabama's $8.9M Round 4 requires applicants to articulate evidence-based practices with training, supervision, and fidelity plans — MORE training rides as a subcontract line (capped at 10% of award) in ADMH-certified treatment providers' proposals.
portal: PAPER ONLY — 1 original + 2 copies + 1 USB physically received by 2:00 pm CT at ADMH Contracts & Purchasing, Montgomery; email/fax not accepted
accounts_needed: Partner needs AL SoS registration, E-Verify, STAARS vendor registration, ADMH certification
match_required: None stated; no supplanting; indirect capped 15%
page_limit: New proposals: cover 1 + org 2 + program 5 + budget 2 pp
scoring_map: 100 pts; program description 30 (EBPs clearly articulated w/ fidelity + training + supervision plans = Section III(e), the MORE slot); understanding 20; experience 15; readiness 15; budget 20

name: Sedgwick County / Wichita KS opioid settlement RFPs (4 programs)
funder: Sedgwick County + City of Wichita, KS
program: OUD Treatment/Recovery/Prevention RFPs 26-0080..83 (Kansas Fights Addiction Act local share)
heart: For-profits check a box on the response form and apply directly — and RFP 26-0081's Workforce Support goal ($580K, awards to $200K) explicitly funds 'continuing education and skill-building training' for behavioral-health clinicians. A straight MORE training proposal.
portal: Email submission to Purchasing@sedgwick.gov (RFP number in subject) — no portal registration
page_limit: No hard limits; per-question word guides
scoring_map: 100 pts: understanding/methodology 25; qualifications 20; evidence-based practices 20 (MORE's RCT base); cost 15; performance measures 10; accessibility 10

name: Williamson County TN opioid settlement — CY27 cycle
funder: Williamson County Opioid Task Force (admin: MTSU OPSR)
program: Annual community abatement grants under TN Opioid Abatement Council strategies
heart: For-profits are explicitly eligible to apply directly, and remediation item FF4 funds 'training providers to offer multi-modal, evidence-informed treatment of pain' — MORE training for Williamson County clinicians is a verbatim allowable activity. Open now, due Aug 17.
page_limit: No page limit; per-section character limits in the portal
scoring_map: 100 pts: program design 15 (EBPs); budget justification 20 (line items tied to activity codes — cite FF4/AA9/BB15); need 10; goals 10; capacity 10

name: York County PA opioid settlement — 2027 cycle
funder: York County Board of Commissioners (admin: York County Planning Commission)
program: Annual settlement grants, Exhibit E uses; 17 rounds over 18 years
heart: York County settlement dollars explicitly fund treatment, recovery, and training under Exhibit E — a MORE cohort for York County SUD clinicians is a direct remediation use. Open now but GATED: required info sessions already ran.
page_limit: Work plan ≤2 pp; support letters ≤3 pp

name: PCORI — Addressing Substance Use (Cycle 3 2026)
program: Topical PFA — comparative clinical-effectiveness research on substance use
heart: The cleanest research fit we've found: a head-to-head trial of MORE vs CBT (or MORE + usual care/MOUD) for opioid use disorder is exactly what this funds — and for-profits can apply directly. Opened today; the LOI gate is Sep 9.
accounts_needed: PCORI Online account; realistically an academic/clinical trial partner
scoring_map: Merit review; must map to the PFA's substance-use CER priorities with a substance-use primary outcome. Position MORE against CBT/usual care for OUD + co-occurring chronic pain.

name: Virginia OAA — locality grants (FY27 final new-award window 10/27 / FY28 apps due 3/2/2027)
heart: Every VA city and county has a settlement allocation it can only unlock by getting an abatement project approved. Get MORE named as the evidence-based training contractor in locality applications before the 10/27/2026 final new-FY2027 cutoff, or in FY2028 new applications (due 3/2/2027).
portal: OAA Grants Portal (voaagrants.us) — held by the locality; MORE enters via the locality's contractor budget
